scope_of_spec: Express application bootstrap: middleware registration, route mounting, error handling, and server startup. Does not contain business logic.
overview: The HTTP Server component is the entry point of the url-pulse process. It creates and configures an Express application, registers JSON body-parsing middleware, mounts the Check Handler routes (POST /check) and History Handler routes (GET /history, GET /history/:id), registers a global error-handling middleware, and binds the server to a TCP port derived from the PORT environment variable (default 3000). This component is thin by design — it wires together other components but contains no business logic.
responsibilities: Register express.json() middleware for JSON request body parsing.
Import and mount the Check Handler router at the root path.
Import and mount the History Handler router at the root path.
Register a catch-all 404 handler for unrecognised routes.
Register a global Express error-handling middleware (4-argument signature) that formats error responses as JSON.
Read PORT from process.env (default: 3000) and start the HTTP server.
Export the Express app instance for use in integration tests without starting the server.

apis.name: POST /check
apis.description: Delegated entirely to C-2 Check Handler router. Mounted by this component.

apis.name: GET /history
apis.description: Delegated entirely to C-3 History Handler router. Mounted by this component.

apis.name: GET /history/:id
apis.description: Delegated entirely to C-3 History Handler router. Mounted by this component.

behavior: On process start, instantiate the Express app.
Register express.json() as the first middleware so all routes receive parsed JSON bodies.
Import the Check Handler Express Router (from C-2) and call app.use(checkRouter).
Import the History Handler Express Router (from C-3) and call app.use(historyRouter).
Register a 404 handler after all routes: respond with { error: 'Not Found' } and status 404.
Register a global error handler (err, req, res, next) that responds with { error: err.message } and status err.status ?? 500.
Read PORT from process.env.PORT; if absent or non-integer, default to 3000.
Call app.listen(port) and log a single startup message to stdout: 'url-pulse listening on port <port>'.
Export the Express app instance so integration tests can call supertest(app) without starting the server.
edge_cases: PORT environment variable is set to a non-integer string (e.g., 'abc'): the server must fall back to port 3000 and not crash.
A route handler throws a synchronous error: the global error handler must catch it and return a JSON error response with status 500, not crash the process.
A request arrives for a path that does not match any registered route (e.g., GET /ping): the 404 handler must respond with { error: 'Not Found' } and HTTP 404.

express.json() receives a body with invalid JSON syntax: Express automatically returns HTTP 400 with a SyntaxError; the global error handler should format this as { error: '<message>' } with status 400.
constraints_and_considerations: This component must contain zero business logic — it is a wiring layer only.
The app instance must be exported separately from the listen() call to support test isolation.
No authentication or authorization middleware is registered (C-4 NFR).
TypeScript strict mode must be enabled; all Express handler signatures must be correctly typed.
The server must be ready to accept connections within 2 seconds of process start on a standard development machine (NFR-3).
Design decision (resolved): PORT defaults to 3000, overridable via process.env.PORT. Justification: conventional Express default; zero configuration for local development.
Design decision (resolved): express.json() is used without a size limit for this iteration. A limit can be added later without breaking changes.
